title: Domestic (LT-I) tariff schedule, effective 1 April 2026
text: This schedule applies to all domestic (LT-I) connections in the Nalgarh and Sirupur circles with effect from 1 April 2026 and replaces the schedule dated 1 April 2024. Energy charges are telescopic and are set per billing month: 0 to 100 units at ₹3.40 per unit, 101 to 250 units at ₹5.15 per unit, 251 to 400 units at ₹6.90 per unit, and above 400 units at ₹8.25 per unit. Because domestic meters are read every two months, the slab limits are doubled for a bimonthly bill, so the first 200 units of a two-month bill are charged at ₹3.40 per unit, the next 300 units at ₹5.15, and so on. The fixed charge is ₹45 per kW of sanctioned load per month, with a minimum of ₹45 per month for any connection, including a locked house with zero consumption. Electricity duty of 6 percent is levied on energy charges only, not on fixed charges. A fuel and power purchase cost adjustment (FPPCA) is applied quarterly and shown as a separate line on the bill; for July to September 2026 it is 18 paise per unit. Lifeline consumers whose consumption stays at or below 50 units per month are billed at a flat ₹1.75 per unit with no fixed charge, but if consumption crosses 50 units in any month the entire bill for that period is charged at the normal slab rates.

title: Domestic (LT-I) tariff schedule, effective 1 April 2024 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 April 2026 by the current domestic tariff schedule. This page is kept for reference because bills for consumption before 1 April 2026 were calculated on it. Energy charges were telescopic per billing month: 0 to 100 units at ₹3.10 per unit, 101 to 200 units at ₹4.80 per unit, 201 to 400 units at ₹6.40 per unit, and above 400 units at ₹7.90 per unit. The fixed charge was ₹40 per kW of sanctioned load per month. Electricity duty was 5 percent of energy charges. Lifeline consumers using up to 50 units per month were billed at ₹1.50 per unit. For bimonthly bills the slab limits were doubled in the same way as today. Changeover rule: where a two-month billing period includes days both before and after 1 April 2026, total consumption is split between the old and new schedules in proportion to the number of days in each, and both calculations are shown on the bill. Consumers who believe the split was calculated wrongly can ask for a recalculation at their section office within 60 days of the bill date.

title: Bill dates, due dates and delayed payment surcharge
text: Domestic consumers are billed every two months; commercial (LT-II) and industrial consumers are billed monthly. The due date is printed on the bill and is 15 days from the bill date for domestic connections and 10 days for commercial connections. A delayed payment surcharge (DPS) of 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid amount is added from the day after the due date, worked out per day of delay, with a minimum surcharge of ₹20. The DPS appears on the following bill. Holiday rule: if the printed due date falls on a Sunday or a public holiday, a payment on the next working day is treated as on time only at cash counters. Online payments must be completed by 11:59 pm on the printed due date, because the online channels are open every day. A prompt payment rebate of 1 percent of energy charges, capped at ₹100, is given when a domestic bill is paid in full within 5 days of the bill date through any digital channel. Bills that are not received can be downloaded from the app or website using the 12-digit consumer number; non-receipt of a bill is not accepted as a reason to waive the DPS.

title: Payment channels and limits, effective 1 January 2026
text: Bills can be paid through the Vellora Energy app, the website, any UPI app using the 12-digit consumer number, net banking, debit and credit cards, and at 46 cash collection counters across the two circles. Credit card payments carry a convenience fee of 0.9 percent of the amount plus GST, charged by the payment gateway; UPI, net banking and debit card payments are free. Cash is accepted only for bills up to ₹10,000; anything above that must be paid digitally or by demand draft drawn in favour of Vellora Energy Distribution Ltd. This limit replaces the earlier ₹50,000 cash limit set by the 2023 collection circular. Cheques are accepted at counters for domestic bills only. A dishonoured cheque attracts a penalty of ₹500 plus the delayed payment surcharge, and after two dishonoured cheques in 12 months the account is barred from paying by cheque for one year. Payments made through third-party apps can take up to 2 working days to show on the account, but the time stamp on the payment receipt is treated as the payment date when the surcharge is worked out.

title: Cash collection circular VED/COM/2023/14 (superseded)
text: Circular VED/COM/2023/14, dated 3 March 2023, is superseded by the payment channel rules that took effect on 1 January 2026, and is kept here only for reference. Under this circular, cash payments were accepted up to ₹50,000 per bill at all collection counters, and cheques were accepted at counters for both domestic and commercial bills. A dishonoured cheque attracted a penalty of ₹250, and there was no bar on future cheque payments after a dishonour. Counter hours under the circular were 9 am to 4 pm on working days and 9 am to 1 pm on the first and third Saturdays. Credit card payments at that time were accepted only on the website, with a convenience fee of 1.1 percent. Collection agents were required to issue a printed receipt for every cash payment and to deposit collections at the sub-division office by 5 pm the same day. Consumers paying arrears of more than ₹25,000 needed the approval of the assistant engineer before the counter could accept the payment.

title: Disconnection for non-payment and reconnection
text: If a bill remains unpaid 15 days after the due date, a disconnection notice is sent by SMS and as a printed notice, and supply may be disconnected after a further 7 days. Disconnections are not carried out after 4 pm, on Sundays or on public holidays. To reconnect, all dues including the delayed payment surcharge must be paid. The reconnection fee is ₹125 for single-phase connections and ₹350 for three-phase connections, and it is added to the next bill rather than collected upfront. Supply is restored within 6 hours of payment in Nalgarh city and within 24 hours elsewhere. If a connection stays disconnected for more than 6 months, the supply agreement is terminated, the security deposit is adjusted against the dues, and a fresh connection application with full charges is needed. A part payment does not stop a disconnection unless an instalment plan has been approved by the section officer. Instalment plans allow arrears above ₹5,000 to be paid in up to 3 monthly instalments, and are allowed once in any 24-month period.

title: New domestic connection: documents, charges and timelines
text: Applications for a new domestic connection can be made online or at the section office. Documents needed: proof of ownership or occupancy, which can be a sale deed, a property tax receipt, or a registered rent agreement with owner's NOC; a photo ID; and a wiring completion certificate from a licensed electrical contractor. Charges for a single-phase domestic connection up to 5 kW are an application fee of ₹50, a service connection charge of ₹1,500, and a refundable security deposit of ₹800 per kW of sanctioned load. Three-phase domestic connections above 5 kW and up to 20 kW have a service connection charge of ₹4,000 and the same deposit rate. The connection is released within 7 working days in Nalgarh and Sirupur towns and within 15 working days in rural areas, where no network extension is needed. Where a new pole or line extension is required, the cost is estimated separately and the connection is released within 30 days of payment of the estimate. The security deposit earns interest at the bank rate, credited every year on the April bill.

title: New commercial (LT-II) connection: documents, charges and timelines
text: This page covers shops, offices, clinics and other non-domestic premises up to 50 kW. Documents needed: proof of ownership or a registered lease, a photo ID of the proprietor or authorised signatory, a trade licence or shop and establishment registration, and a wiring completion certificate from a licensed electrical contractor. Charges for a single-phase commercial connection are an application fee of ₹100, a service connection charge of ₹3,000, and a refundable security deposit of ₹2,000 per kW of sanctioned load. Three-phase commercial connections have a service connection charge of ₹6,500 and the same deposit rate. Commercial connections are released within 10 working days in towns and 20 working days in rural areas where no network extension is needed. A commercial connection cannot be released at a residential address unless the owner has a mixed-use approval from the municipality. Commercial consumers are billed monthly, and the security deposit is reviewed every April against the average of the last 12 bills; any shortfall is billed as an additional deposit.

title: Rooftop solar for domestic consumers: net billing, effective 1 October 2025
text: From 1 October 2025, new domestic rooftop solar systems are connected under net billing, not net metering. Under net billing, every unit you import from the grid is charged at the normal domestic tariff, and every unit you export is credited at a fixed rate of ₹2.85 per unit. Exports therefore do not cancel imports one for one. This replaces net metering, under which exports offset imports unit for unit; systems commissioned before 1 October 2025 stay on net metering until 30 September 2032. The maximum system size is 10 kW or the sanctioned load, whichever is lower. The application fee is ₹1,000, and the bidirectional meter costs ₹3,600, paid by the consumer. Export credits are adjusted against later bills. Any credit still unused on 31 March each year will lapse, with no payout and no carry-forward into the next financial year. A system can be commissioned only after inspection by the section engineer, which is done within 15 working days of the installer's completion report.

title: Planned and unplanned outages, and compensation
text: Planned maintenance shutdowns are announced at least 48 hours in advance by SMS and in local newspapers, and each shutdown is limited to 6 hours between 9 am and 5 pm. Unplanned outages can be reported on the 24-hour helpline 1800 425 7766, by SMS to 56070, or in the app; every report gets a complaint number. Under Vellora's standards of performance, if supply to an individual consumer is not restored within 4 hours in towns or 12 hours in rural areas after the fault is reported, the consumer is entitled to ₹50 for each additional 6 hours or part of it, up to ₹500 per incident. Compensation is not automatic: it must be claimed in writing or through the app within 30 days of the outage, quoting the complaint number. Compensation is not payable for outages caused by storms declared a natural calamity, by faults in the consumer's own wiring, or during load shedding ordered by the state grid. Approved compensation is credited on the next bill.

title: Meter accuracy testing on request
text: Consumers who suspect a faulty meter can ask for it to be tested by paying a testing fee of ₹200 for single-phase meters and ₹500 for three-phase meters. Testing is done at the premises with a reference meter within 10 working days, and the consumer or a representative may be present. If the consumer disputes the site result, the meter can be sent to the accredited laboratory at Sirupur for an extra ₹300. A meter is treated as accurate if its error is within plus or minus 1 percent for smart meters, or plus or minus 2 percent for older electromechanical meters. If the meter is found running fast beyond the limit, the testing fee is refunded and bills for up to the previous 6 months are revised. If it is found running slow beyond the limit, Vellora may recover the shortfall for up to 3 months only. While a test is pending, the consumer must keep paying the average of the last 3 undisputed bills to avoid disconnection.

title: Prepaid smart meters
text: Prepaid smart meters are being installed across Nalgarh city since 2025 and are optional elsewhere. Prepaid consumers get a rebate of 2 percent on energy charges. The minimum recharge is ₹200, and recharges can be made in the app, through UPI or at any cash counter. Low balance alerts are sent by SMS at ₹300 and at ₹100. When the balance goes below zero, supply is not cut immediately: an emergency credit of ₹150 or 3 days, whichever runs out first, is allowed automatically. Supply is never cut between 6 pm and 9 am, on Sundays or on public holidays; disconnection for a negative balance happens only between 10 am and 1 pm on working days, and supply returns within 15 minutes of a recharge. Daily fixed charges are deducted from the balance at midnight. Any unused balance is refunded within 30 days if the connection is closed. Switching back to a postpaid meter is allowed after 12 months on prepaid, with a meter change fee of ₹500.

title: Name change and ownership transfer
text: To change the name on a connection after a purchase or an inheritance, submit the transfer form with the sale deed or a legal heir certificate, a photo ID, and a no-dues certificate for the connection. The fee is ₹100 for domestic and ₹500 for commercial connections. Tenants cannot have an existing connection transferred into their own name; a tenant can only be added as an alternate contact for SMS alerts and bill reminders, and the connection stays in the owner's name. Transfers are processed within 7 working days. The existing security deposit moves to the new owner only if the previous owner signs a consent letter; otherwise the new owner pays a fresh deposit and the old deposit is refunded to the previous owner. When the transfer follows the death of the registered consumer, the fee is waived if the application is made within 6 months of the date of death; after 6 months the normal fee applies. Name corrections for spelling mistakes are free and are handled at the section office.

title: Customer care centres, hours and helplines
text: Customer care centres are at Station Road in Nalgarh, the Collectorate Complex in Sirupur, and the Kanhai and Ralegaon sub-division offices. They are open 9:30 am to 5:30 pm, Monday to Saturday, and are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Cash counters close at 4:30 pm. The Nalgarh centre stays open until 7 pm on the last two working days of each month, for bill payments only. The 24-hour helpline 1800 425 7766 is for outages and safety emergencies only; billing queries on the helpline are handled from 8 am to 8 pm, and calls about bills outside those hours are asked to call back. Complaints not resolved within 15 days can be taken to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum at Sirupur. After a decision by the forum, a consumer who is still not satisfied may approach the state Electricity Ombudsman within 30 days of the forum's order. There is no fee for filing a complaint with either the forum or the ombudsman.
